title: 229. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Finding Intersection Points of Algebraic Curves
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Intersection of a parabola and a horizontal line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection points of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=4\).
questions.question: Find all intersection points of the curves \(y=x^2\) and \(y=4\).
questions.explanation: Set the two expressions for \(y\) equal: \(x^2=4\). Then \(x=2\) or \(x=-2\). For each \(x\), \(y=4\). Therefore the intersection points are \((-2,4)\) and \((2,4)\).
questions.hint: Equate the two expressions for \(y\), then solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Intersection of a line and a parabola
questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection points of \(y=x+1\) and \(y=x^2-1\).
questions.question: Find all intersection points of \(y=x+1\) and \(y=x^2-1\).
questions.explanation: Set \(x+1=x^2-1\). Rearranging gives \(x^2-x-2=0\), so \((x-2)(x+1)=0\). Thus \(x=2\) or \(x=-1\). If \(x=2\), then \(y=3\). If \(x=-1\), then \(y=0\). Therefore the intersection points are \((2,3)\) and \((-1,0)\).
questions.hint: Equate the expressions, solve the quadratic, and substitute each \(x\)-value to find \(y\).

questions.concept: Intersection of a parabola and a line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection points of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=2x+3\).
questions.question: Find all intersection points of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=2x+3\).
questions.explanation: Set \(x^2=2x+3\). Rearranging gives \(x^2-2x-3=0\), so \((x-3)(x+1)=0\). Thus \(x=3\) or \(x=-1\). If \(x=3\), then \(y=9\). If \(x=-1\), then \(y=1\). Therefore the intersection points are \((3,9)\) and \((-1,1)\).
questions.hint: Equate the two expressions for \(y\), factor the quadratic, and find the corresponding \(y\)-values.

questions.concept: Intersection of a circle and a line through the origin
questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection points of \(x^2+y^2=25\) and \(y=x\).
questions.question: Find all intersection points of the circle \(x^2+y^2=25\) and the line \(y=x\).
questions.explanation:
Substitute \(y=x\) into \(x^2+y^2=25\): \(x^2+x^2=25\), so \(2x^2=25\). Thus \(x^2=\frac{25}{2}\), giving \(x=\pm\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}\). Since \(y=x\), the intersection points are
\[
\left(\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2},\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\left(-\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2},-\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)
\]
questions.hint: Substitute \(y=x\) into the circle equation, then solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Intersection of a parabola and a line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection points of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=x+2\).
questions.question: Find all intersection points of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=x+2\).
questions.explanation: Set \(x^2=x+2\). Rearranging gives \(x^2-x-2=0\), so \((x-2)(x+1)=0\). Thus \(x=2\) or \(x=-1\). If \(x=2\), then \(y=4\). If \(x=-1\), then \(y=1\). Therefore the intersection points are \((2,4)\) and \((-1,1)\).
questions.hint: Equate the two expressions for \(y\) and solve the resulting quadratic equation.

questions.concept: Intersection of a circle and a line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection points of \(x^2+y^2=10\) and \(y=3x\).
questions.question: Find all intersection points of the circle \(x^2+y^2=10\) and the line \(y=3x\).
questions.explanation: Substitute \(y=3x\) into \(x^2+y^2=10\): \(x^2+9x^2=10\), so \(10x^2=10\). Thus \(x^2=1\), giving \(x=1\) or \(x=-1\). If \(x=1\), then \(y=3\). If \(x=-1\), then \(y=-3\). Therefore the intersection points are \((1,3)\) and \((-1,-3)\).
questions.hint: Substitute the line equation into the circle equation, then solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Intersection of a parabola and the \(x\)-axis
questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection points of \(y=x^2-4\) and \(y=0\).
questions.question: Find all intersection points of the curve \(y=x^2-4\) and the \(x\)-axis \(y=0\).
questions.explanation: Set \(x^2-4=0\). Then \(x^2=4\), so \(x=2\) or \(x=-2\). Since \(y=0\), the intersection points are \((-2,0)\) and \((2,0)\). The point \((0,-4)\) is the \(y\)-intercept, not an \(x\)-intercept.
questions.hint: Set \(y=0\) in the parabola equation and solve for \(x\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection points of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=-x^2+8\).
questions.question: Find all intersection points of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=-x^2+8\).
questions.explanation: Set \(x^2=-x^2+8\). Then \(2x^2=8\), so \(x^2=4\). Thus \(x=2\) or \(x=-2\). For each \(x\), \(y=x^2=4\). Therefore the intersection points are \((2,4)\) and \((-2,4)\).
questions.hint: Equate the two expressions for \(y\), then solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Intersection of a cubic curve and a line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection points of \(y=x^3\) and \(y=x\).
questions.question: Find all intersection points of \(y=x^3\) and \(y=x\).
questions.explanation: Set \(x^3=x\). Rearranging gives \(x^3-x=0\), so \(x(x^2-1)=0\). Thus \(x=0\), \(x=1\), or \(x=-1\). Since \(y=x\), the intersection points are \((0,0)\), \((1,1)\), and \((-1,-1)\).
questions.hint: Set the two expressions equal, factor completely, and find every real solution.

questions.concept: Tangent intersection of a parabola and a line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection points of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=2x-1\).
questions.question: Find all intersection points of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=2x-1\).
questions.explanation: Set \(x^2=2x-1\). Rearranging gives \(x^2-2x+1=0\), so \((x-1)^2=0\). Thus \(x=1\) is the only solution. Then \(y=1^2=1\). Therefore the curves intersect at exactly one point, \((1,1)\).
questions.hint: Equate the expressions, solve the resulting quadratic, and note whether the two curves are tangent.
